phases.sub: Resolve the KB id and start ingestion per data source
phases.does: The attendee found their own Knowledge Base without being handed an id to paste, and asked it to read the HR, customer and finance documents. Re-running this is safe — it re-reads the same documents and settles on the same result.
phases.cmd:
# KB ID — shown at the end of the previous step, or resolve it directly here:
KB_ID=$(aws bedrock-agent list-knowledge-bases --region us-east-1 \
  --query 'knowledgeBaseSummaries[?name==`workshop-kb`].knowledgeBaseId | [0]' --output text)
echo "KB_ID=$KB_ID"

for DS in $(aws bedrock-agent list-data-sources \
              --knowledge-base-id "$KB_ID" \
              --region us-east-1 \
              --query 'dataSourceSummaries[].dataSourceId' \
              --output text); do
  aws bedrock-agent start-ingestion-job \
    --knowledge-base-id "$KB_ID" \
    --data-source-id "$DS" \
    --region us-east-1
done

phases.does: The documents are really in the Knowledge Base, so the agents will answer from the company's own content instead of from an empty index. Because the newest run is reported rather than an arbitrary one, a stale success from an earlier attempt cannot pass for this one.
phases.cmd:
for DS in $(aws bedrock-agent list-data-sources \
              --knowledge-base-id "$KB_ID" \
              --region us-east-1 \
              --query 'dataSourceSummaries[].dataSourceId' \
              --output text); do
  echo "=== Data source $DS ==="
  aws bedrock-agent list-ingestion-jobs \
    --knowledge-base-id "$KB_ID" \
    --data-source-id "$DS" \
    --region us-east-1 \
    --query 'sort_by(ingestionJobSummaries, &startedAt)[-1].[status,startedAt]' \
    --output text
done
phases.expected: every line shows COMPLETE with a timestamp from the sync just started

phases.sub: Load the Vault root token into the shell
phases.does: The attendee is in the same shell and on the same machine that deployed Vault, and now holds administrator access for the checks that follow. If this fails, they know immediately they are in the wrong place rather than mid-way through a confusing failure.

phases.step: Step 1 — Confirm pods are Running
phases.does: All three Vault servers are up, not one or two, so the cluster can pick a leader and hand out credentials. Knowing there are three also matters later, because only the server that handled a request will have written it down.
phases.cmd: kubectl get pods -n vault
phases.expected: vault-0, vault-1, vault-2 and vault-agent-injector all 1/1 Running

phases.step: Step 2 — Confirm KMS auto-unseal
phases.does: Vault is open and will answer requests, and it opened itself using AWS KMS — so nobody has to hold or type unseal keys during the workshop, and a restarted pod comes back on its own.
phases.cmd: kubectl exec -n vault vault-0 -- vault status
phases.expected: Seal Type awskms, Initialized true, Sealed false

phases.step: Step 3 — Confirm Raft peers
phases.does: The three servers formed one cluster with an elected leader rather than sitting alone, so the secrets they store are replicated and losing a single server does not take Vault down.
phases.cmd:
kubectl exec -n vault vault-0 -- \
  sh -c "VAULT_TOKEN='${VAULT_ROOT_TOKEN}' vault operator raft list-peers"
phases.expected: three peers, vault-0 leader, vault-1 and vault-2 followers, all voters

phases.step: Step 4 — Confirm audit device
phases.does: Vault is writing down every request it handles, so at the end of each use case the attendee can go and find their own request in the log. Without this there would be nothing to find.
phases.cmd:
kubectl exec -n vault vault-0 -- \
  sh -c "VAULT_TOKEN='${VAULT_ROOT_TOKEN}' vault audit list"
phases.expected: at least one audit device listed

phases.step: Step 5 — Confirm Vault Enterprise + the Agent Registry

phases.cmd:
kubectl delete pod oidc-check -n verify-access --ignore-not-found --now >/dev/null 2>&1
kubectl run oidc-check --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -n verify-access \

kubectl delete pod oidc-check -n verify-access --now >/dev/null 2>&1

pkill -f "kubectl port-forward -n vault svc/vault 8200:8200" 2>/dev/null; \
  kubectl port-forward -n vault svc/vault 8200:8200 >/dev/null 2>&1 & \
  sleep 2 && \
  export VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200 && \
  VAULT_TOKEN=$(jq -er '.root_token' ~/vault-init.json) && export VAULT_TOKEN && \
  echo && echo "Vault Web UI: $VAULT_ADDR/ui" && echo "Root token:   $VAULT_TOKEN" \
  || echo "ERROR: no root token in ~/vault-init.json — the Tier-2 deploy has not run on this machine"

athena_query() {
  local Q="$1"
  local QID=$(aws athena start-query-execution --work-group workshop \
    --query-string "$Q" --query 'QueryExecutionId' --output text)
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    STATE=$(aws athena get-query-execution --query-execution-id "$QID" \
      --query 'QueryExecution.Status.State' --output text)
    [ "$STATE" = "SUCCEEDED" ] && break
    [ "$STATE" = "FAILED" ] && { aws athena get-query-execution \
      --query-execution-id "$QID" --query 'QueryExecution.Status.StateChangeReason' --output text; return 1; }
    sleep 2
  done
  aws athena get-query-results --query-execution-id "$QID" --output json \
    | jq -r '.ResultSet.Rows[] | [.Data[] | (.VarCharValue // "" | if . == "" then "-" else . end)] | @tsv' \
    | column -t -s $'\t'
}

phases.step: Set up the query helpers
phases.does: The rest of the page reads as one command per question, pointed at the log catalog in your own deploy region.
phases.cmd:
# The Glue catalog + Athena 'workshop' workgroup were provisioned in YOUR deploy
# region (resolved from Terraform state — never a hardcoded literal, per the region
# contract). Point the CLI at that region so the workgroup and the workshop_logs
# database resolve regardless of your shell's default region.
export AWS_REGION="$(terraform -chdir=infrastructure output -raw region)"

# Run a query in the 'workshop' workgroup, wait for it, echo the execution id
athena_run() {
  local QID=$(aws athena start-query-execution --work-group workshop \
    --query-string "$1" --query 'QueryExecutionId' --output text)
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    local S=$(aws athena get-query-execution --query-execution-id "$QID" \
      --query 'QueryExecution.Status.State' --output text)
    [ "$S" = "SUCCEEDED" ] && { echo "$QID"; return 0; }
    [ "$S" = "FAILED" ] && { aws athena get-query-execution --query-execution-id "$QID" \
      --query 'QueryExecution.Status.StateChangeReason' --output text >&2; return 1; }
    sleep 2
  done
}

# Multi-row aligned table
athena_query() { aws athena get-query-results --query-execution-id "$(athena_run "$1")" \
  --output json | jq -r '.ResultSet.Rows[] | [.Data[] | (.VarCharValue // "-")] | @tsv' | column -t -s $'\t'; }

# Single row, vertical (field -> value)
athena_record() { aws athena get-query-results --query-execution-id "$(athena_run "$1")" \
  --output json | jq -r '.ResultSet.Rows as $r | range(0; ($r[0].Data|length)) as $i
    | "\($r[0].Data[$i].VarCharValue)\t\($r[1].Data[$i].VarCharValue // "-")"' | column -t -s $'\t'; }

# First value only (capture into a variable)
athena_scalar() { aws athena get-query-results --query-execution-id "$(athena_run "$1")" \
  --query 'ResultSet.Rows[1].Data[0].VarCharValue' --output text; }
